channel_sources:
- conda-forge
channel_targets:
- conda-forge main
docker_image:
- quay.io/condaforge/linux-anvil-x86_64:alma10
python_min:
- '3.11'

about.description:
A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that gives a language model a
sandboxed mathematical subset of SageMath: 40 stateful tools for symbolic
calculus, algebra, number theory, graphs, groups, elliptic curves, plotting
and claim verification. Each MCP session gets a dedicated Sage worker
process, so variables, functions and assumptions persist across tool calls.
Caller code is deny-by-default: a name is refused unless the generated
allowlist offers it or the caller's own code bound it.

A SageMath runtime is REQUIRED at run time and is deliberately not a
dependency of this package: `sage` must be on PATH (conda-forge ships
`sage`, which is the usual way to get it), or the pip extra
`sagemath-mcp[passagemath]` can supply one. Making Sage a hard dependency
would force a multi-gigabyte install on users who run the project's
hardened container instead.
about.summary: Model Context Protocol server that provides stateful SageMath computations.

name: sagemath-mcp
raw_meta_yaml:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/prefix-dev/recipe-format/main/schema.json
schema_version: 1

# The conda-forge recipe, in the v1 (`recipe.yaml`) format defined by CEP 13/14.
# staged-recipes marked the v0 `meta.yaml` format deprecated in August 2026 and
# says v0 submissions are "less likely to be reviewed in a timely manner", so
# this is the format the submission uses and therefore the one kept here.
#
# `tests/test_conda_recipe.py` keeps it honest against `pyproject.toml`: the
# runtime dependencies, the Python floor, the entry point, and the source hash
# against PyPI. The version trails the project between a bump and the upload
# that follows it, because the hash can only exist after the release ships.

context:
  name: sagemath-mcp
  version: "0.9.3"
  # conda-forge's global `python_min` is 3.11, and this package requires 3.12.
  # Without this override the build environment gets 3.11 and pip refuses the
  # install outright: "Package 'sagemath-mcp' requires a different Python:
  # 3.11.16 not in '>=3.12'". Setting it in the recipe context is how a package
  # raises the floor above the global pin; it flows into the host requirement,
  # the run requirement and the test matrix below, so there is one number.
  python_min: "3.12"

package:
  name: ${{ name|lower }}
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  url: https://pypi.org/packages/source/${{ name[0] }}/${{ name }}/sagemath_mcp-${{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: f8afd37b7a6e31c56d6f095b7ce91fc0356883d1175251fa8ca4af6cd5a46173

build:
  noarch: python
  script: ${{ PYTHON }} -m pip install . -vv --no-deps --no-build-isolation
  number: 0
  python:
    entry_points:
      - sagemath-mcp = sagemath_mcp.server:main

requirements:
  host:
    - python ${{ python_min }}.*
    - hatchling >=1.32.0
    - pip
  run:
    - python >=${{ python_min }}
    # 4.0.8 is the floor this package is tested against; conda-forge has
    # carried it since late September 2026 (4.0.10 on 2026-09-26).
    - fastmcp >=4.0.8,<5
    - pydantic >=2.13.4
    - anyio >=4.14.2

tests:
  - python:
      imports:
        - sagemath_mcp
      pip_check: true
      # Both ends of the supported range: a noarch package installs on every
      # Python at or above python_min, so testing only the floor would miss a
      # break on the newest one. conda-forge's linter asks for this.
      python_version:
        - ${{ python_min }}.*
        - "*"
  - requirements:
      run:
        - python ${{ python_min }}.*
    script:
      # `--help` is the only command that works without a SageMath runtime;
      # every evaluation needs one, and this package deliberately does not
      # depend on Sage (see about/description).
      - sagemath-mcp --help

about:
  homepage: https://github.com/XBP-Europe/sagemath-mcp
  summary: Model Context Protocol server that provides stateful SageMath computations.
  description: |
    A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that gives a language model a
    sandboxed mathematical subset of SageMath: 40 stateful tools for symbolic
    calculus, algebra, number theory, graphs, groups, elliptic curves, plotting
    and claim verification. Each MCP session gets a dedicated Sage worker
    process, so variables, functions and assumptions persist across tool calls.
    Caller code is deny-by-default: a name is refused unless the generated
    allowlist offers it or the caller's own code bound it.

    A SageMath runtime is REQUIRED at run time and is deliberately not a
    dependency of this package: `sage` must be on PATH (conda-forge ships
    `sage`, which is the usual way to get it), or the pip extra
    `sagemath-mcp[passagemath]` can supply one. Making Sage a hard dependency
    would force a multi-gigabyte install on users who run the project's
    hardened container instead.
  license: MIT
  license_file: LICENSE
  documentation: https://github.com/XBP-Europe/sagemath-mcp/blob/main/USAGE.md
  repository: https://github.com/XBP-Europe/sagemath-mcp
